passages.text: The point of what we are saying is this: We do have such a high priest, who sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven, and who ministers in the sanctuary and true tabernacle set up by the Lord, not by man.
passages.sermon:
We have a high priest.
This high priest is Jesus.
Jesus sat down at the right hand of the throne of God in heaven.
He serves in the holy place.
He serves in the true tabernacle.
The Lord set up this true tabernacle.
A man did not set up this tabernacle.
passages.original: Κεφάλαιον δὲ ἐπὶ τοῖς λεγομένοις τοιοῦτον ἔχομεν ἀρχιερέα ὃς ἐκάθισεν ἐν δεξιᾷ τοῦ θρόνου τῆς Μεγαλωσύνης ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς τῶν ἁγίων λειτουργὸς καὶ τῆς σκηνῆς τῆς ἀληθινῆς ἣν ἔπηξεν ὁ Κύριος οὐκ ἄνθρωπος

passages.text: And since every high priest is appointed to offer both gifts and sacrifices, it was necessary for this One also to have something to offer.
passages.sermon:
Every high priest has a special role.
God appoints each high priest to offer gifts.
God appoints each high priest to offer sacrifices.
Jesus is also a high priest.
Jesus must have something to offer.
passages.original: Πᾶς γὰρ ἀρχιερεὺς εἰς τὸ προσφέρειν δῶρά τε καὶ θυσίας καθίσταται ὅθεν ἀναγκαῖον ἔχειν τι καὶ τοῦτον ὃ προσενέγκῃ

passages.text: Now if He were on earth, He would not be a priest, since there are already priests who offer gifts according to the law.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is our high priest.
If Jesus were on earth, He would not be a priest.
There are already priests on earth.
These priests offer gifts according to the law.
passages.original: εἰ μὲν οὖν ἦν ἐπὶ γῆς οὐδ’ ἂν ἦν ἱερεύς ὄντων τῶν προσφερόντων κατὰ νόμον τὰ δῶρα

passages.text: The place where they serve is a copy and shadow of what is in heaven. This is why Moses was warned when he was about to build the tabernacle: “See to it that you make everything according to the pattern shown you on the mountain.”
passages.sermon:
The priests serve in a place that is only a copy of what is in heaven.
Their service is a shadow of heavenly things.
God warned Moses before he built the tabernacle.
God said, “See to it that you make everything according to the pattern shown you on the mountain.”
passages.original: οἵτινες ὑποδείγματι καὶ σκιᾷ λατρεύουσιν τῶν ἐπουρανίων καθὼς κεχρημάτισται Μωϋσῆς μέλλων ἐπιτελεῖν τὴν σκηνήν Ὅρα γάρ φησίν Ποιήσεις πάντα κατὰ τὸν τύπον τὸν δειχθέντα σοι ἐν τῷ ὄρει

passages.text: Now, however, Jesus has received a much more excellent ministry, just as the covenant He mediates is better and is founded on better promises.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the mediator of a new covenant.
This covenant is better than the old covenant.
God gave this new covenant with better promises.
Jesus now has a much more excellent ministry.
He serves as the mediator of this better covenant.
passages.original: Νυνὶ δὲ διαφορωτέρας τέτυχεν λειτουργίας ὅσῳ καὶ κρείττονός ἐστιν διαθήκης μεσίτης ἥτις ἐπὶ κρείττοσιν ἐπαγγελίαις νενομοθέτηται

passages.text: For if that first covenant had been without fault, no place would have been sought for a second.
passages.sermon: The first covenant was not perfect.\r\nIf the first covenant had no fault, God would not have made a second covenant.\r\nGod made a second covenant because the first one was not enough.
passages.original: εἰ γὰρ ἡ πρώτη ἐκείνη ἦν ἄμεμπτος οὐκ ἂν δευτέρας ἐζητεῖτο τόπος

passages.text: But God found fault with the people and said: “Behold, the days are coming, declares the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.
passages.sermon:
God saw fault in the people.
God spoke about this.
The Lord said, “The days are coming.
I will make a new covenant.
I will make this covenant with the house of Israel.
I will make this covenant with the house of Judah.”
passages.original: μεμφόμενος γὰρ αὐτοὺς λέγει Ἰδοὺ ἡμέραι ἔρχονται λέγει Κύριος καὶ συντελέσω ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον Ἰσραὴλ καὶ ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον Ἰούδα διαθήκην καινήν

passages.text: It will not be like the covenant I made with their fathers when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, because they did not abide by My covenant, and I disregarded them, declares the Lord.
passages.sermon:
God spoke about a new covenant.
God said this new covenant will not be like the old covenant.
God made the old covenant with the ancestors of Israel.
God took the ancestors of Israel by the hand.
God led them out of the land of Egypt.
The ancestors of Israel did not remain faithful to God's covenant.
God disregarded them because they broke His covenant.
The Lord declares these things.
passages.original: οὐ κατὰ τὴν διαθήκην ἣν ἐποίησα τοῖς πατράσιν αὐτῶν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ἐπιλαβομένου μου τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῶν ἐξαγαγεῖν αὐτοὺς ἐκ γῆς Αἰγύπτου ὅτι αὐτοὶ οὐκ ἐνέμειναν ἐν τῇ διαθήκῃ μου κἀγὼ ἠμέλησα αὐτῶν λέγει Κύριος

passages.text: For this is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after those days, declares the Lord. I will put My laws in their minds and inscribe them on their hearts. And I will be their God, and they will be My people.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the people of Israel.
God promised a new covenant.
God said this would happen after certain days.
God said, “I will make this covenant with the house of Israel.”
God said, “I will put My laws into their minds.”
God said, “I will write My laws on their hearts.”
God said, “I will be their God.”
God said, “They will be My people.”
passages.original: ὅτι αὕτη ἡ διαθήκη ἣν διαθήσομαι τῷ οἴκῳ Ἰσραὴλ μετὰ τὰς ἡμέρας ἐκείνας λέγει Κύριος διδοὺς νόμους μου εἰς τὴν διάνοιαν αὐτῶν καὶ ἐπὶ καρδίας αὐτῶν ἐπιγράψω αὐτούς καὶ ἔσομαι αὐτοῖς εἰς Θεόν καὶ αὐτοὶ ἔσονταί μοι εἰς λαόν

passages.text: No longer will each one teach his neighbor or his brother, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’ because they will all know Me, from the least of them to the greatest.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about His new covenant with Israel.
God says people will not need to teach their neighbors about Him.
People will not need to tell their brothers, “Know the Lord.”
Everyone will know God.
The least important people will know God.
The most important people will know God.
All people, from the least to the greatest, will know Him.
passages.original: καὶ οὐ μὴ διδάξωσιν ἕκαστος τὸν πολίτην αὐτοῦ καὶ ἕκαστος τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ λέγων Γνῶθι τὸν Κύριον ὅτι πάντες εἰδήσουσίν με ἀπὸ μικροῦ ἕως μεγάλου αὐτῶν

passages.text: For I will forgive their iniquities and will remember their sins no more.”
passages.sermon: God speaks to the people of Israel.\r\nGod promises to forgive their iniquities.\r\nGod will not remember their sins anymore.
passages.original: ὅτι ἵλεως ἔσομαι ταῖς ἀδικίαις αὐτῶν καὶ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν οὐ μὴ μνησθῶ ἔτι

passages.text: By speaking of a new covenant, He has made the first one obsolete; and what is obsolete and aging will soon disappear.
passages.sermon:
God spoke of a new covenant.
God made the first covenant obsolete.
The first covenant is now old.
What is old and aging will soon disappear.
passages.original: Ἐν τῷ λέγειν Καινὴν πεπαλαίωκεν τὴν πρώτην τὸ δὲ παλαιούμενον καὶ γηράσκον ἐγγὺς ἀφανισμοῦ
